judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's arithmetic is right on every item. I recomputed all seven repaired values independently: F(2) - F(5) = 4 - 25 = -21 (id 1); [x^3-4x] from 1 to 3 = 15 - (-3) = 18 (id 2); [t^3+2t] from 0 to 2 = 12 (id 3); the integral from 6 to 4 is -(10 - 3) = -7 (id 4); -cos(pi/3) + cos(0) = 1/2 (id 5); G(x) = -integral from 5 to x, so G'(2) = -(2^2+1) = -5 (id 6); and with u = x^2+1 the bounds run 1 to 5, giving (625-1)/8 = 78 (id 7). Eight find-and-fix problems are present, the three named error families each recur, and the study guide's three sections map one-to-one onto the worksheet's three skill tags. Where the judge did not look is the seam between what the worksheet prints as an answer slot and what verify.json actually covers, and there the packet has a real gap. Problem 4 prints two lettered parts - '(a) Say which integral the value 7 actually is' and '(b) Give the correct value of the integral from 6 to 4' - and verify.json id 4 is a single eval returning -7; part (a)'s answer (the integral from 4 to 6, i.e. the difference of the two givens) has no entry. Problem 5 asks 'State the correct antiderivative' before evaluating, and the only entry is the definite_integral returning 0.5; -cos x is never bound. Problem 6(a) asks the student to 'Rewrite G(x) with the variable at the upper bound' and problem 7(a) asks 'Convert the bounds to u and state the new interval' (u from 1 to 5); neither has an entry. This is not a nitpick about style, because the file itself proves the fix was available: problem 2 DOES carry a second entry, {"type":"integrate","expr":"3*x**2 - 4","expected":"x**3 - 4*x"}, under the same id, exactly so that its part (a) is bound. The pattern was applied once and skipped four times. Separately, the worksheet's own directions box says 'In each problem: name the error in words first, then show corrected work', and none of problems 1-7 carries a manual entry for that named diagnosis; gate_log.txt reports '8 passed - 0 failed - 1 manual', which describes a sheet with one open item rather than seven diagnosis slots plus one essay.

strengths_to_preserve: Every planted trap is an expression that reproduces the wrong method rather than a hand-typed number. Id 2's trap is '(3**3 - 4*3) - 1**3 - 4*1', which literally performs the dropped-parenthesis subtraction; id 7's is '(2**4 - 0**4)/8', which evaluates the u-antiderivative at the x-bounds. The verifier proves each is distinguishable from the correct value, so the 'Common wrong answers' block in the key is generated evidence, not an author's guess.

Problem 3's trap value is 14, which is exactly f(upper bound) = 3(2)^2+2. The final response names that as 'the answer that equals f(upper bound), which is that error's fingerprint', so a teacher who sees 14 on a paper can diagnose the dummy-variable error from the number alone. Designing the wrong answer to be self-identifying is worth keeping.

The sheet's error families are cleanly separated and then recombined: bounds order (1, 4, 6, 7), the parentheses/sign slip (2, 5), and the dummy variable (3), with problem 7 sitting at the intersection because a substitution changes the variable AND the bounds. The final response's page counts (worksheet 5, key 4, study guide 2) match pdfinfo on all three files.

root_causes.description: Lettered sub-parts that print their own answer demand were not given their own verify entries. Problem 2 received a companion integrate entry for its part (a); problems 4(a), 5, 6(a) and 7(a) make the same kind of demand and received nothing, so the delivered key's quick-answer bank shows one value where the worksheet asked for two.
evidence: verify.json id 2 carries two entries (definite_integral 18 and integrate 'x**3 - 4*x'), demonstrating the multi-entry pattern
worksheet.pdf problem 7: '(a) Convert the bounds to u and state the new interval. (b) Evaluate the integral correctly.' - verify.json id 7 has one definite_integral entry
answer_key.pdf Quick Answers prints '7. 78' with no trace of the u-interval [1, 5] the item asked for

root_causes.description: In a misconception-analysis format the named diagnosis is the assessed skill, and here seven diagnoses are folded inside machine-verified ids. The worksheet's directions box requires the student to 'name the error in words first', yet only problem 8 is recorded as manual, so gate_log.txt and final_response.md both describe a sheet with a single open item.
evidence: worksheet.pdf directions: 'In each problem: name the error in words first, then show corrected work.'
verify.json: ids 1-7 are definite_integral/integrate/eval; only id 8 is {"type":"manual"}

improvements.title: Lettered sub-parts (4a, 5, 6a, 7a) print answer demands with no verify entry
improvements.proposed_change: Make lettered parts a first-class unit of the verification contract. When a worksheet stem contains '(a)', '(b)', '(c)' markers, require one verify entry per marker under that id and fail the gate on a shortfall. For this packet: id 4 needs an entry pinning part (a)'s answer (the integral from 4 to 6 as the difference of the two givens); id 5 needs an integrate entry for -cos(x); id 6 needs an entry for the sign-flipped rewrite; id 7 needs an entry for the transformed bounds u = 1 to u = 5 - the exact shape problem 2 already uses.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture: worksheet.tex with a stem containing '(a)' and '(b)' and a verify.json with a single entry under that id. The gate must fail with 'problem N: 2 lettered parts, 1 entry'. Adding the second entry passes. This fixture passes today.
improvements.expected_impact: The quick-answer bank stops under-reporting: a grader sees the u-interval and the antiderivative the sheet asked for, not just the final number, and no printed demand ships unchecked.
improvements.risk: Low. Lettered markers are easy to detect in the tex source, and an explicit per-id override handles the rare part that genuinely needs no separate answer.

improvements.title: Seven find-and-fix diagnoses are delivered inside machine-verified ids
improvements.proposed_change: In misconception-analysis mode, require every find-and-fix id to carry BOTH a machine entry for the repaired value AND a manual entry for the named diagnosis, and have SKILL.md say so explicitly for that instructional mode. The manual entry's desc should reuse the trap's own desc text so the grader gets the target diagnosis for free. gate_log.txt would then report 8 manual items for this sheet, and final_response.md would describe the sheet honestly.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture: a verify.json declaring instructional mode misconception-analysis with a trap on id 1 and no manual entry under id 1. verify.py must exit non-zero asking for the diagnosis companion. Adding it passes. Today the fixture passes as fully machine-verified.
improvements.expected_impact: The assessed skill in an error-analysis sheet - naming the error - stops being reported as machine-checked when nothing checked it, and the teacher's manual-review list matches the sheet's actual demands.
improvements.risk: Low. It raises manual counts on one instructional mode only; the risk is verbosity in the key, mitigated by generating the manual desc from the existing trap desc.

case_summary: A very good misconception sheet that earned its 32/32 on content. Eight find-and-fix items cover the three named error families (bounds order and sign, the lost parentheses around F(a), the dummy variable), each planted wrong result is a declared trap whose expression reproduces the wrong method, and the verifier proved every trap distinguishable from the correct value. I recomputed all seven repaired values (-21, 18, 12, -7, 1/2, -5, 78) and confirmed them, and the three stated page counts match pdfinfo. The defect the judge missed is in the verification contract rather than the mathematics: four lettered sub-parts that print their own answer demand - 4(a)'s identification of the integral, 5's correct antiderivative, 6(a)'s sign-flipped rewrite, 7(a)'s transformed u-bounds - have no verify entry, while problem 2's part (a) does, which shows the multi-entry pattern was available and simply not applied. On top of that the directions box requires a named diagnosis in words on every problem, and only problem 8 is recorded as manual, so the gate's '8 passed, 1 manual' line understates what a teacher still has to read.
